_about: Atlas's additions to rela's description: rules the current rela cannot hold, because it refuses unknown keys in schema.yaml. State merges this file into the description it answers, key by key; Control applies the rules for any kind. Data, not code: no BEAM module names a kind. Per kind: create.ask = the only fields a create form asks for; create.id = how the id is made: prefix plus the next free number, zero-padded to digits; or from a property (from), whose value must match pattern, with template filled from its groups ({1}, {2}, ...) after replace, in lower case when lower is true, and error when it does not match; the same value always makes the same id; nobody ever types or changes an id, nor the property it is made from; create.defaults = values for the fields create does not ask; properties.<name>.set_by = a field only a connector or the system fills (never in a form, shown only when it has a value); properties.<name>.multiline = true for text of several lines and sections (a form edits it in a multi-line editor; the line breaks are kept); properties.<name>.label = the name a page shows for the field instead of its own. progress = how far an item is, worked out from the items under it on every read, never stored, and shown in lists instead of its own field: over = the relation whose items point at it, field = the property that says how far such an item is (for a kind without a rule of its own), own = its own property, shown while nothing is under it. The top-level progress gives the order of the values (least far first; the least far child wins), done_label = what a list shows for an item that is completed itself (never because its children are), to_test = the value and label of an item whose children are all completed while it is not. completion = how an item is completed, worked out on every read, never stored: one way or a list of ways, any of which completes it: by = it has a link through that association (someone accepted it); over, field, value = an item pointing at it through that relation has that value (one of its pull requests is merged); through, field, value = an item it points at through that relation has that value. primary = the property that names a fact in a list and on its page (when it is empty, the property the id is made from names it); connector = an outside system's connector fills this kind, read-only: system (which connector), address (the property that says where the outside thing is), fields (property: the outside system's field it is copied from), until (property: values; a fact with one of these values is read no more). Per relation: relations.<name>.parent = true for a relation by which a fact belongs under another (at most one; its page goes back there, a create adds under it); every other relation is an association, a concept a kind has by being in its from (accepted_by: completable), shown with the fact that set it and set through its own form; relations.<name>.set_by = an association only a migration or connector sets: shown, never in a form, refused by Control. relations.<name>.only_target = only a client that is one of the facts the association points at sets or removes it, and only to itself (error says why to anyone else; also = clients that may anyway, such as the migration); actions.set and actions.remove = the label and key of the page's action that does so (Accept until it is set, Reopen after, on the same key; remove asks for a note); requires_completed_children = set is refused while a fact under it is not completed ({key}, {children}); closes_parent = a new fact under one that has the link, by a create or a move, is refused ({parent}, {kind}). Per kind: top = false for a kind that is not on the start page, reached only through the facts that point at it. Per type: types.<name>.format = "url" for values that are web addresses (rela has no such type); Control offers to open a fact's first such field in a browser. relations.<name>.limit = how many facts may point at one parent through it, counting only those whose field is one of values (max, field, values); a new link (a create under the parent, or a move to it) is refused when that many are there already, with error, where {parent}, {child} and {value} (the label of its field's value) are filled in; links that are there already stay. Agent records (UC-Atlas-19): agent = "request" or "step" names the kinds the agent keeps its requests and steps in (the agent never puts them as tools); start = {key, label} puts an action on the start page that opens the kind's list (with top = false, the kind itself is not there); order = "newest" lists a kind newest first; by_hand = false: no keys to make, change or delete one (the agent writes it); properties.<name>.cause = true or a title: an item page lists the facts of this kind whose field holds the item's key; relations.<name>.add = false: a page lists the facts of that relation without an action to add one; actions = [{key, label, to, when}]: more actions on a fact's page, only while its fields have one of the values in when; a to of agent:<intent> asks the agent (the TUI's : with that intent) instead of opening a page.

limit.error: {parent} already has {child} ({value}); an issue is one change: close that PR first, or make a new issue

accepted_by.closes_parent: {parent} is accepted; reopen it first, or put this under another {kind}

id.error: name must start with a letter, e.g. Melle
url must be a GitHub pull request URL, e.g. https://github.com/eyra/atlas/pull/12
